list_entry.title: An assumption made in the explanation

A.explanation:
Too Strong/Specific: Most Out of Scope: Agree

The author isn't talking about whether 51% or more viewers can agree on the #1 most disturbing part of an opinion or analysis. This is way too specific.

Negating it doesn't really change the conversation: "sorry, author, only 49% of viewers can agree on what was the #1 most disturbing part of an opinion or analysis."

C.explanation:
The author doesn't have to assume that every single TV viewer has at least one fringe opinion.

Would it hurt the argument if we said, "Hey, author, there is this one viewer, Lenny, and all of his opinions are inside the political mainstream"? Not at all.

D.explanation:
Out of Scope: Other Types of Shows

The author doesn't need to assume that economic forces have more impact on talk shows than on other types of shows. Other types of shows aren't even being talked about.

E.explanation: Just because we talked about talk shows being similar when it comes to the blandness of opinions doesn't mean that the author is assuming that talk shows are similar in most other ways.
